name: ssh-keygen
description: Creates SSH key pairs for passwordless, encrypted authentication.

flags.description: Key type: ed25519 (modern, preferred) or rsa 4096 (legacy compatibility).
Label, conventionally an email or purpose.
Fingerprint of a key (verify which key is which).

examples.output:
Generating public/private ed25519 key pair.
Enter passphrase (empty for no passphrase):
Your identification has been saved in /home/user/.ssh/id_ed25519
examples.explanation: Creates a modern key pair: id_ed25519 (PRIVATE — never leaves this machine) and id_ed25519.pub (shared with servers).
RSA-4096 for old systems that do not support ed25519.
Shows the fingerprint — how you confirm which key is which on GitHub or servers.

about: Ed25519 is the current best choice: small, fast, secure. RSA-4096 remains for legacy targets. A passphrase on the private key protects it if your laptop is stolen; ssh-agent caches the unlocked key per session. Private keys must be chmod 600 — ssh refuses world-readable keys.
mistakes: Committing or sharing the PRIVATE key (no .pub extension).
Generating 1024-bit RSA keys — obsolete and rejected by modern servers.
warnings: A private key without passphrase on a compromised laptop is an instant breach of every server it reaches. Use a passphrase plus ssh-agent.
